one_liner: Data enrichment and GTM workflow automation platform for sales teams
blocker: API/HTTP API access reportedly requires a paid plan (~$495/mo after Explorer tier removal); official docs cover only narrow table-lookup API key usage

evidence.claim: Clay issues a self-serve API key from account settings used for integrations
evidence.quote: Under `Account`, locate `API key`. You'll find your API key here for integrations.

evidence.claim: The documented Clay API key enables narrow native operations (row lookups across tables)
evidence.quote: A Clay API key is required for all Clay-native integrations.

evidence.claim: Clay's HTTP API feature moves data in/out of Clay tables via any REST endpoint and methods
evidence.quote: you can pull external data into your Clay table or push data out from Clay using any endpoint and method (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE).

evidence.claim: HTTP API access was moved to a $495/mo plan after the free Explorer tier was removed
evidence.quote: Clay killed the Explorer tier, moved HTTP API access to $495/mo, if you want HTTP API access, you're at $495 minimum.

evidence.claim: Clay ships a first-party MCP server alongside its public API, with OAuth 2.0 and short-lived bearer tokens
evidence.quote: Clay MCP and the Clay Public API have overlapping but not identical coverage. MCP owns Audiences querying, natural-language account Q&A, and

notes: Most official docs describe Clay's HTTP API as an outbound connector (Clay calling other APIs), not Clay's own inbound public API surface; OAuth 2.0 and 24-hour bearer tokens are reported only by a third-party review (pipeline.zoominfo.com). The first-party 'Clay MCP' server is evidenced only via a third-party blog (scalekit.com), not vendor docs in the supplied material. Pricing reportedly changed in 2025-2026 (Explorer tier killed), so free-tier API access is likely unavailable.
